title: Canary Quality Watchdog and Auto-Reversion Engine
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a Canary Quality Watchdog (CQW) that continuously scores canary and A/B cohorts against multidimensional evaluation signals and triggers automated reversion policies when quality regressions exceed configurable thresholds. This ticket covers the scoring model, integration with the traffic-split controller, rollback arbitration logic, and operator-facing controls (mute, manual revert, dry-run). The goal is to reduce time-to-detect regressions from model/config rollouts and eliminate manual rollback lag for high-impact regressions while preserving an easy manual override path.
acceptance_criteria: CQW produces a per-cohort quality score every 60s for canary and experiment cohorts
Automated reversion triggers when composite score degrades by >6% vs baseline for 3 consecutive windows or when any high-severity slice fails SLOs
Rollback executes via traffic controller API and records a GitHub deployment rollback PR + console audit event
Operators can opt to run CQW in dry-run mode (alerts only) and mute individual signals
End-to-end E2E test simulating a model drift that causes automated rollback in CI with a reproducible fixture
tasks: Design composite scoring: weight token-level BLEU-like metric, semantic-similarity regression, hallucination rate, latency P95
Implement per-slice telemetry ingestion from Console metrics pipeline
Add scoring service that emits decisions to rollout-controller topic
Extend traffic-split controller to accept revert commands and support staged reversion (50% -> 0%)
Create operator UI: enable/disable CQW, configure thresholds, view audit timeline
Write runbook: when CQW reverts, how to investigate, how to re-promote safely

notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) cadence vs sensitivity — settled on 60s rolling windows with 3-window confirmation to reduce flapping; 2) composite score vs single-signal triggers — composite score preferred for fewer false positives but high-severity slices (security/regulatory prompts) can bypass and force immediate revert; 3) rollback hysteresis to avoid oscillations: enforce cool-down 10m after revert.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Li): prefer explicit per-release baseline anchoring rather than rolling baseline to avoid gradual drift masking
ML Infra (Priya Menon): scoring should use cached embeddings and batch similarity computations to keep costs low
Reliability (Marcus Hill): require traffic-controller idempotency guarantees before enabling auto-revert in prod
